proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- hasCart -- the agent is holding/pushing a shopping cart
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Demonstration 1 (required items: a1):
  0: {at(0,7)} E
  1: {at(1,7)} INTERACT
  2: {at(1,7), hasCart} N
  3: {at(1,6), hasCart} N
  4: {at(1,5), hasCart} N
  5: {at(1,4), hasCart} N
  6: {at(1,3), hasCart} E
  7: {at(2,3), hasCart} E
  8: {at(3,3), hasCart} INTERACT
  9: {at(3,3)} N
 10: {at(3,2)} N
 11: {at(3,1)} INTERACT
 12: {at(3,1)} S
 13: {at(3,2)} S

 16: {at(3,4), hasCart} S

 24: {at(8,7), hasCart} E

 26: {at(10,7), hasCart} E
 27: {at(11,7), hasCart} EXIT
 28: {at(11,7), hasCart} <terminal>

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: The shopper is obliged to have a cart at some point during the trip.
The shopper is prohibited from exiting the store without a cart.
The shopper is prohibited from being at cell (3,1) while holding a cart.
The shopper is prohibited from interacting at cell (3,1) while holding a cart.
The shopper is prohibited from moving while holding a cart in the upper cells (3,1) or (3,2).
The shopper is prohibited from moving north from cell (3,3) while holding a cart.
Whenever the shopper reaches cell (3,3) with a cart, they are obliged to put the cart down.
After visiting cell (3,1), the shopper is obliged to regain a cart before the trip ends.

parsed.text: Shopping carts are prohibited in single-file aisles, identified by a corridor width of one cell in either direction.
Carts may not be taken into aisles where shelves are directly on both sides of the shopper.
It is forbidden to move a cart into a narrow shelf aisle that is intended for pedestrians only.

Carts may only be parked or released in wide open aisle space where they do not block shelves or a narrow passage.
After returning from a pedestrian-only shelf aisle to the cart bay, the shopper is obliged to retrieve the parked cart.

accepted.description: [g1_no_carts_between_shelves] FORBIDDEN: (hasCart ∧ betweenOpposingShelves)  where betweenOpposingShelves := ((shelfE ∧ shelfW) ∨ (shelfN ∧ shelfS))

[g1_no_enter_cart_incompatible_aisle] FORBIDDEN: enterCartIncompatibleAisle  where cartIncompatibleAisle := (singleFileAisle ∧ adjShelf); singleFileAisle := freeWidthH≤1; enterCartIncompatibleAisle := (hasCart ∧ MOVE) · cartIncompatibleAisle

[g1_park_at_narrow_aisle_mouth] OBLIGED: after arriveWithCartAtNarrowAisleMouth, eventually ¬hasCart (before exit)  where cartAtNarrowAisleMouth := (narrowAisleMouth ∧ hasCart); narrowAisleMouth := (at(3,3) ∧ wideOpenAisle); wideOpenAisle := (freeWidthH>2 ∧ freeWidthV>2 ∧ ¬adjShelf); arriveWithCartAtNarrowAisleMouth := (hasCart ∧ MOVE) · cartAtNarrowAisleMouth

[g1_reclaim_parked_cart] OBLIGED: after parkCartAtBay, eventually retrieveCartAtBay (before exit)  where cartAtBay := (cartBay ∧ hasCart); cartBay := at(3,3); noCartAtBay := (cartBay ∧ ¬hasCart); parkCartAtBay := (cartAtBay ∧ INTERACT) · noCartAtBay; retrieveCartAtBay := (noCartAtBay ∧ INTERACT) · cartAtBay
[g1_hands_free_shelf_pick] FORBIDDEN: (hasCart ∧ INTERACT ∧ shelfPickSlot)  where shelfPickSlot := (singleFileAisle ∧ adjShelf); singleFileAisle := freeWidthH≤1

[g1_park_only_wide_open] FORBIDDEN: (parkCart ∧ ¬legalCartParkingArea)  where legalCartParkingArea := (wideEnoughForCartParking ∧ ¬adjShelf); wideEnoughForCartParking := (freeWidthH>2 ∧ freeWidthV>2); parkCart := (hasCart ∧ INTERACT) · ¬hasCart

[g1_retrieve_after_return_from_pedestrian_aisle] OBLIGED: after returnFromPedestrianAisleToBay, eventually retrieveCartAtBay (before exit)  where cartAtBay := (cartBay ∧ hasCart); cartBay := at(3,3); noCartAtBay := (cartBay ∧ ¬hasCart); pedestrianShelfAisle := (adjShelf ∧ freeWidthH≤1); retrieveCartAtBay := (noCartAtBay ∧ INTERACT) · cartAtBay; returnFromPedestrianAisleToBay := (pedestrianShelfAisle ∧ ¬hasCart ∧ MOVE) · noCartAtBay
